review_notes: I read the whole file and the definition of `closedCell_zero_eq_singleton` in Basic.lean. I grepped for other uses of `OneSkeletonGraph`; the only file that mentions it is the target. The `@[simps]`-generated lemmas (`vertexSet`, `edgeSet`, `IsLink`) and `adj_iff` look consistent with each other. They normalise to the `closedCell 0 x ∪ closedCell 0 y` form, and `isLink_iff_pair` is correctly left non-simp. The one concern is the non-simp status of `closedCell_zero_eq_singleton`. It is a design choice, so my confidence is moderate. I could not check how the change would affect the rest of Mathlib or whether it would loop, and I did not run Lean.

findings.declaration: Topology.CWComplex.OneSkeletonGraph.exists_isLoopAt_iff_subsingleton (and the structure proof) — use of RelCWComplex.closedCell_zero_eq_singleton
findings.problem: `closedCell_zero_eq_singleton` is not a simp lemma. This file therefore passes it by name to `simp` and `simp_rw` five times: lines 37, 64, 66 and 68, plus the `rw` at line 52. The canonical form of a 0-cell closure is the singleton `{map 0 j ![]}`. The lemma is an unconditional equation with a fixed direction. It cannot loop, because the right-hand side contains no `closedCell`. Without the attribute, a plain `simp` cannot reduce `closedCell 0 x` to the form in which `Set.union_singleton`, `Set.singleton_union` and `Set.pair_eq_pair_iff` apply. The same explicit passing recurs in Basic.lean (line 462), so this is a pattern in the library and not a quirk of this file.
findings.proposed_change: Consider tagging `RelCWComplex.closedCell_zero_eq_singleton` (and its `CWComplex` alias) with `@[simp]` in Basic.lean. Then drop the explicit `closedCell_zero_eq_singleton` arguments from the `simp` calls in this file, for example `simp [hx]` and `simp [hxy]`. If the attribute is judged too aggressive, add a local `attribute [local simp]` or a dedicated simp lemma for the pair form. Keep `isLink_iff_pair` as the explicit conversion lemma.
findings.benefit: Proofs about 1-skeleton graphs would reach the singleton and pair normal form automatically. Call sites would no longer need to know which unfolding lemma to supply. Closure of 0-cells would be handled consistently across CW-complex files.
